evidence.text: thread
Pictograph of a hand (又) holding a group of threads (糸) that are connected together (系).
繋也。从糸丿聲。凡系之屬皆从系。

Ideogrammic compound (會意 /会意): abbreviated 手 + 糸. Also used as simplified forms:
* Simplified from 繫 (𣪠 → 丿) (through an intermediate form 毄).
* Simplified from 係 (elimination of 人).
繋也。从糸丿聲。凡系之屬皆从系。

Etymological analysis: pictographic
Someone 亻 who connects 系 people; 系 also provides the pronunciation
Phonosemantic compound. 亻 represents the meaning and 系 represents the sound.
絜束也。从人从系，系亦聲。

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *keːɡs): semantic 人 + phonetic 系 (OC *ɡeːɡs).
The simplified form 系 also exists as a traditional character, and is also used to simplify 繫. In ancient times, 系, 係, and 繫 were usually interchangeable graphic variants, although in some compounds, only one form is acceptable (e.g. 世系 and 繋辭／繋辞).
The meaning “yes” in Cantonese and Hakka is likely an independently created sound symbolism, only associated with this character by folk etymology.

evidence.field: 形義通解；甲骨、金文、小篆字例；《說文》條目
evidence.text: The entry reports oracle-bone and bronze forms of 系 as a hand (爪/又) holding connected silk, interpreted as binding or connection. It notes an alternative proposal that 系 is an early form of 攣, and says the small-seal 丿 may be a reduced 爪; on this analysis 說文's 丿-as-phonetic explanation is doubtful. The entry reports oracle-bone uses as a ritual name, place/state name, and later bronze personal name; Warring States 系 also writes 奚 in some texts. It describes 系 as extended from connection to lineage, citing 《漢書·高帝紀》 “漢帝本系，出自唐帝.” The entry's account distinguishes graphic origin from those loans/uses; it does not date the cited inscriptions individually.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「系」

evidence.field: 《說文》; 形義通解; cited classical texts
evidence.text: The entry records 說文's analysis of 係 as “絜束也。从人从系，系亦聲,” and describes oracle-bone 係 as 人 plus 糸, interpreted as binding a person with a cord; some forms add 又 hands. It reports a verb use in oracle-bone inscriptions, a bronze personal-name use, and a later form with 人 and 糸 separated, which it identifies as the basis of the small-seal shape. It cites 《易·坎》 “係用徽纆” and 《國語·越語上》 “係妻拏” for binding, 《北史》 for maintaining connection, and 《水滸傳》 for a copular use; it does not establish a date for each cited textual stratum.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「係」

evidence.field: 《說文》; 形義通解; cited classical texts
evidence.text: The entry gives 說文's account of 繫 as 糸 plus phonetic 毄 and glosses its original sense as tying/fastening. It cites 《禮記·禮器》 for tying an animal, 《禮記·月令》 for imprisonment, 《荀子·勸學》 for hanging a nest, 《周禮·天官·大宰》 for connecting people to states, and 張衡《西京賦》 for a relation/dependence sense. These citations illustrate separate senses but do not alone establish their chronological order; the dictionary supplies no dated manuscript evidence here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「繫」

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The 係 entry records the Great Xu 說文 text as “絜束也。从人，从系，系亦聲” and Duan Yucai's version as “从人，系聲.” It lists meanings including bind, a cord for tying, connection/concern, and ‘be’; its examples include 國語·越語上 and Jia Yi's 過秦論. This confirms a historical phonetic account for 系 within 係, while the modern and later meanings remain distinct from the graph's formation story.
evidence.title: [A00165] 係 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.field: Character information; Shuowen; Guangyun; Kangxi quotations
evidence.text: The 系 record provides seal-script and bronze-script image links, lists traditional-character correspondences 係 and 繫, and reproduces 說文 “系：繋也。从糸丿聲.” It gives Guangyun's “緒也” and Kangxi quotations connecting 系 with 繫, continuity, lineage and descent. The accessible page is useful for the received lexicographic record, but does not resolve whether early 丿 was a phonetic or a graphic reduction of a hand.
evidence.title: 系 - Chinese Text Project

evidence.text: The authors' 2014 table documentation identifies MC as a transcription of medieval dictionary evidence, not a reconstruction, and OC as reconstruction in the Baxter–Sagart system. Local table rows provided in the research packet give 系 MC hejH, OC *[m]-kˤek-s; 係 MC kejH, OC *kˤek-s; and 繫 readings MC kejH, OC *Cə.kˤe-s and MC hejH, OC *m-kˤek-s. These are local-file observations, not extracted from the opened page. The system's own documentation supports keeping its notation and MC/OC columns distinct; it does not itself establish a component relationship.

evidence.field: 甲金文字形；《說文》；形義通解；早期用例
evidence.text: The entry interprets 系’s oracle-bone and bronze forms as a hand (爪/又) holding connected silk, with a binding/connection sense. It records alternatives: a proposal that 系 is an early form of 攣, and the received 說文 analysis 从糸、丿聲. CUHK argues instead that seal-script 丿 is a reduced 爪 and calls the phonetic analysis doubtful. It cites oracle-bone ritual-name and place/state-name uses and a bronze personal-name use, but does not date those inscriptions individually.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「系」

evidence.text: The entry gives 系’s received 《說文》 analysis as 从糸、丿聲, and identifies 係 with modern Mandarin xì and Guangyun 胡計. Its account interprets the 係 oracle-bone graph as 人 plus 糸, sometimes with hands, for binding a person; it describes 係 as a verb in oracle-bone inscriptions and notes a later bronze arrangement of 人 and 糸 that it considers the basis of the seal form. This source evidence supports a phonetic role for 系 within 係 separately from disputed claims about 系’s own origin.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「係」

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry reports 《說文》’s 係 analysis “絜束也。从人从系，系亦聲” and provides a variant discussion, including a claim that some written forms arose through scribal confusion of 人 and 彳 or through a 糸 variant. This is evidence for the received phonetic account, not a resolution of 系’s paleographic origin.
evidence.title: [A00165] 係 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.field: 《說文》；《禮記》《荀子》《周禮》《西京賦》 examples
evidence.text: The entry gives 繫’s received formation as 糸 plus phonetic 毄 and glosses its early sense as tying/fastening. It lists textual examples for confinement, hanging, concern, connection, and relation/dependence. These cited texts illustrate senses but do not by themselves establish a dated sequence of semantic change or a historical graphic simplification into 系.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「繫」

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry identifies 繫 as 糸 with phonetic 毄 and gives readings xì and jì with senses including connect, hang, concern, imprison, and tie. It lists 系 as a variant/counterpart. The page supports a modern orthographic relationship in its variant list but does not establish a historical chronology for that relationship.

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: The primary source search found a substantive disagreement for 系: the received 說文 treats 丿 as a phonetic, while the CUHK paleographic dictionary interprets it as a reduced hand shape and rejects that phonetic analysis. No inspected source conclusively settles the earliest form's structure; the dictionary also records a separate proposal that 系 is an early 攣 form.

The dossier's formation-type conflict cannot be reduced to one universally accepted analysis. Current evidence favors describing the attested oracle-bone/bronze graphic interpretation separately from the Han 說文 analysis, with the uncertainty preserved.

系's oracle-bone uses cited by CUHK include ritual name, place/state name and later bronze personal name, but their character functions and exact inscription dates are not independently established in the inspected materials. Do not present those as dated semantic milestones for ‘thread’, ‘lineage’ or ‘system’.

The extension from binding/connection to lineage is explicitly proposed by CUHK with a Han Shu example, but its intermediate chronology is not established. The modern gloss ‘system’ has no historical sequence established here.

係's early ‘bind/tie’ reading is independently supported by the oracle-bone account and classical examples. Its later meanings ‘maintain connection’ and copular ‘be’ are listed, but the semantic transitions and earliest dated attestations for each are not established by this research.

繫 has received Shuowen and classical senses including tie, confine, hang, connect and concern; the inspected page does not document a dated paleographic sequence or establish whether those forms were graphically borrowed/interchangeable with 系 at each stage. No claim about 系 being a regular graphic simplification of 繫 is established here.

For 系 as the proposed phonetic in 係, sources explicitly assign a phonetic role (Shuowen and MOE); CUHK also documents compatible related readings. Local Baxter–Sagart readings differ in initial and vocalic detail across 系 (*[m]-kˤek-s, MC hejH) and 係 (*kˤek-s, MC kejH), while 繫 has two readings. The role is source-attested but the exact historical sound development is not resolved here.

Current kMandarin xì is present in all supplied local Unihan rows, but official Unicode character records were inaccessible in this web session; therefore official Unihan click-through verification is unavailable.

Baxter–Sagart exact rows were supplied locally and checked, but no verified official online character-specific table row was opened for the three readings. The accessible authors' PDF describes the system and notation only.
No glyph image was opened or visually inspected. The external text sources describe ancient forms, but this report does not claim independent visual inspection of those forms.

系’s earliest inscriptional forms and their dates were not independently dated in the inspected character entry. Its proposed hand-plus-connected-threads interpretation is a source assertion, while the alternative 攣-origin proposal and the received 說文 丿-as-phonetic account remain in tension; no adjudication is established here.

The reported oracle-bone ritual, place/state, and bronze personal-name uses are not dated milestones for the lexical senses ‘thread’, ‘connection’, ‘lineage’, or ‘system’. CUHK cites a Han Shu lineage example, but intermediate semantic chronology and a historical sequence for ‘system’ remain unestablished.

係 has an early bind/tie interpretation and a source-attested 系 phonetic role. Its later connection and copular uses are cited in textual sources, but their earliest attestation dates and semantic transitions are not established by this research.

繫’s tie, confine, hang, concern, connect, and relation senses are cited from received texts; the inspected entries do not provide dated manuscript attestations that establish their order or demonstrate that 系 is a regular graphic simplification of 繫.

Local Baxter–Sagart readings retain distinct initial/vocalic details for 系 and 係 (and multiple rows for 繫); exact online rows were not opened. Do not merge the local dataset’s notation with other reconstructions or infer a sound change beyond what sources support.
Official Unicode Unihan pages for the three characters could not be accessed, so their local kMandarin xì rows are not externally click-through verified in this report.

The Commons file-description search results were readable, but subsequent direct opens of the Commons pages and upload image URLs failed with cache/access errors. The file records remain source-page leads; no image pixels were inspected.

items.period: Seal-script style; a modern redraw representing the received Shuowen seal form, not an excavated or dated artifact
items.caption: The seal-script form of 系 has a sweeping upper stroke above two enclosed loops and descending strokes. The graphic account of its earliest form is disputed: one interpretation sees a hand holding connected silk, while the received Shuowen analysis treats 丿 as phonetic.
items.alt: Black seal-script form of 系, with a sweeping upper stroke, two looped sections and descending strokes, on a white background.
items.selection_reason: This is the target character’s seal-script form and directly illustrates the disputed analysis of its upper component.
items.rights: Commons description marks the ancient-script representation public domain; modern vector redraw, not an artifact photograph.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; modern redraw of a received historical script form
items.caption: This seal-script form of 係 places a tall, narrow element beside the 系-like form. In the received analysis, 人 and 系 form 係, with 系 also serving as its phonetic; early forms are separately described as 人 with 糸, sometimes with hands.
items.alt: Black seal-script form of 係, with a tall narrow element on the left and a looped, branching form on the right, on a white background.
items.selection_reason: It helps explain the documented phonetic role of 系 within the related character 係 while showing that 係 has its own early graphic account.
items.rights: Commons file description states the SVG representation is public domain; modern vector redraw, not an artifact photograph.

limitations.text: These are modern redrawings of seal-script forms, not images of dated artifacts. The competing accounts of 系’s graphic origin remain unresolved, and these forms alone do not establish a chronological sequence.
